newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Exiled Cambodian prince should seek amnesty - PM.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Cambodian prince should seek amnesty - PM.

text.p: Cambodia's exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh should write to King Norodom Sihanouk, his half-brother, and ask for an amnesty, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Saturday.

Sirivudh, former foreign minister and ex-secretary general of the royalist FUNCINPEC party, was detained for one month last year on charges linked to an alleged plot to assassinate Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of the Cambodian People's Party.
Sirivudh denied the charges but agreed to go into exile in France in December. A Cambodian court later sentenced him to 10 years imprisonment in absentia.
"The prince must write a letter to his majesty the king to ask for amnesty and I think if there is a letter from him ... his majesty will grant him amnesty," Ranariddh told journalists.
Ranariddh, who heads FUNCINPEC and is the king's son, said he and his party would support a royal amnesty but he did not know Hun Sen's position on the matter.
Earlier this month the king granted amnesty to Ieng Sary, leader of a breakaway faction of the Khmer Rouge and foreign minister during its brutal 1975-79 regime.
He and Pol Pot, the group's leader, were sentenced to death in absentia for their roles in the death of more than one million people during the Khmer Rouge's rule.
But Ieng Sary asked for and received the amnesty, at the request of the two premiers, after saying his legal status must be clarified before peace talks with the government could proceed.

"I understand that his majesty will be delighted (to pardon Sirivudh) because we forgave Ieng Sary," said Ranariddh, adding: "Prince Sirivudh never killed anyone so we must give him amnesty. If we do so it is fair to him and FUNCINPEC."
Sirivudh is still a member of parliament and of the FUNCINPEC steering committee.
His French wife and three children live in Cambodia.
